answer: Trust is lent, never owned outright. Each identity parks its bond in a two-key escrow whose second key is held by a custodian drawn at random from established peers, and neither side can release funds alone. A lone seat makes the voyage with one willing partner. A farm of k needs k distinct custodians, none chosen by the attacker, and any custodian cosigning two colluding seats forfeits their half. Custodians rotate each epoch, so stale alliances decay, and the orchard an attacker must cultivate grows faster than the seats it adds before any clone nears the summit.
